reviews.body:
### 🟡 Changes recommended Swarm initialization still panics when the selected socket is unavailable, and remote Docker pulls bypass the URL-safe registry-auth workaround, risking failures for private images.
2 open issues - [Preserve URL-safe registry auth for remote image pulls](https://github.com/FiligranHQ/xtm-composer/pull/231#discussion_r4684196382) · New - [Retry Swarm initialization when the Docker socket is unavailable](https://github.com/FiligranHQ/xtm-composer/pull/231#discussion_r4684196471) · New
What changed in this PR This PR addresses #177 by making Docker and Swarm honor `DOCKER_HOST`, supporting non-default sockets such as those used by Colima and rootless Docker. **Changes:** - Adds shared endpoint resolution that prefers a configured socket, then `DOCKER_HOST`, then the default socket. - Uses the resolved endpoint for both orchestrators while preserving Docker’s startup retry loop. - Avoids passing remote URLs to the Unix compatibility client and adds endpoint-resolution tests. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | `src/​orchestrator/​swarm/​swarm.rs` | Uses shared endpoint resolution and client creation. | | `src/​orchestrator/​docker/​docker.rs` | Adds endpoint helpers, updates client initialization, and tests endpoint precedence. |
Review effort: Balanced

review_comments.body: Setting `compat` to `None` bypasses the URL-safe registry-auth workaround in `pull_image` for TCP/HTTP endpoints. Private-image pulls can therefore fail when Bollard's standard-base64 `X-Registry-Auth` header contains `+` or `/`, the encoding failure covered by `integration_tests.rs::bollard_registry_auth_header_is_rejected_for_some_passwords`. Support remote transports in the compatibility client, or otherwise preserve URL-safe registry-auth encoding for remote pulls.

Swarm still panics if the selected socket does not exist when Composer starts (for example, `DOCKER_HOST=unix:///run/user/1000/docker.sock` before rootless Docker starts). `connect_docker_client` returns the socket error, and this `unwrap()` aborts orchestration before its scheduling loop; there is no retry in `build_orchestrator`. Please make Swarm initialization wait and retry with logged errors, as Docker initialization does, so it recovers when the daemon becomes available.
